consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. With no turn-1 objection to repair, the only thing this turn could get wrong is its account of a world that moved underneath it, so that is what I tested. D-094 went CONTESTED, and the property that matters about a CONTESTED entry is that it leaves nothing behind: I counted in the live register and found sixteen named identifiers, three reserved cells, one PARTLY MET and no 18-of-18 fragment, so none of D-094's five edits landed and this entry's condition-4 statement is right. Two things are worth recording as good practice rather than as findings. The entry says plainly that Codex completed no turn-1 verdict instead of letting the subjects table's Codex column imply otherwise, and I confirmed that absence at the path. And this is the first repair turn in several where the diff drops nothing of substance — the one removed sentence is superseded by a fuller paragraph in the body.
